_comment: Tags, notes and additions for the blocklist catalogue, written for this project.
Most of the catalogue -- names, categories, homepages and addresses -- is
AdGuard's, imported by scripts/import-blocklists.py. Everything in this
file is ours: what each list is good for, which country it serves, and any
list we add that upstream does not carry.
`size` is NOT set here. It is derived from the rule count measured at
import time, so it cannot drift away from the list it describes.
Tag vocabulary, kept small on purpose -- every tag has to answer a
question someone actually asks while choosing a list:
what it blocks  ads trackers telemetry annoyances malware phishing
scam crypto-mining gambling adult piracy bypass
who it is for   starter regional device allowlist
what to expect  strict  (known to break some legitimate sites)
A two-letter tag is a country, and must be declared in `_countries`.
The interface draws it as a flag; the importer rejects an undeclared one,
because a typo would otherwise become a chip that matches nothing.
`_add` holds lists this project carries and upstream does not. They are
validated and measured exactly like the imported ones.

1hosts_lite.note: A balanced everyday list from the 1Hosts family. A good first choice if you want more than AdGuard's own filter without inviting breakage.

1hosts_xtra.note: The aggressive end of 1Hosts, and it says so itself: expect to allowlist things. Only worth it if you are willing to debug the occasional broken site.

adguard_dns_filter.note: AdGuard's own general-purpose list, assembled from their base, tracking and mobile filters. The safe default, and the one Sift enables on a fresh install.

adguard_popup_filter.note: Just the domains behind pop-ups and pop-unders. Small and additive -- pair it with a general list rather than using it alone.

awavenue_ads_rule.note: Targets the advertising SDKs embedded in Android apps rather than websites. Useful on a network with a lot of phones on it.

dan_pollocks_list.note: A long-running, conservatively maintained hosts file. Small, stable and unlikely to surprise you.

hagezi_multinormal.note: The middle of HaGeZi's three general lists and the one most people should start with. Broad coverage, still tuned to keep sites working.

hagezi_pro.note: A step up from HaGeZi Normal with noticeably more coverage. A reasonable default if you are comfortable allowlisting now and then.

hagezi_pro++.note: Aggressive by design. Blocks a great deal, including things some apps depend on -- pick it only if you will notice and fix the fallout.

hagezi_ultimate.note: The strictest HaGeZi list, and not a set-and-forget choice. Overlaps almost everything in Pro++, so run one of them, not both.

oisd_basic.note: OISD's smaller list, built around not breaking things. An excellent first list, and a good companion to a stricter one.

oisd_full.note: OISD's big list. Still curated against false positives, but its own authors note the risk is higher than the small version.

peter_lowe_list.note: One of the oldest ad and tracker host lists there is. Tiny, careful, and almost never the cause of a problem.

shadowwhisperer_tracking_list.note: Tracking only -- analytics, diagnostics, metrics and IP-lookup endpoints. Layer it on top of an ad list rather than in place of one.

steven_blacks_list.note: The widely used unified hosts file, combining adware and malware sources. A dependable single-list setup.

dandelion_sprouts_anti_push_notification.note: Kills the domains behind "allow notifications?" prompts. Narrow and safe; add it to whatever general list you run.

dandelion_sprouts_game_console_adblock_l.note: A handful of ad domains used by game consoles. Almost nothing in it, so it only makes sense alongside a general list.

hagezi_allowlist_referral.note: An allowlist, not a blocklist: it re-enables affiliate and referral links that stricter lists break. Add it under Allowlists, not here.

hagezi_antipiracy_blocklist.note: Blocks streaming and download sites used for copyright infringement. A policy choice for your network, not a security measure.

hagezi_apple_tracker_blocklist.note: Apple's own device telemetry endpoints. Very targeted; some Apple features expect these to resolve, so watch for side effects.

hagezi_gambling_blocklist.note: A very large list of gambling and betting sites. Worth it if that is the point; otherwise it is half a million rules you do not need.

hagezi_oppo_realme_tracker_blocklist.note: Telemetry endpoints baked into OPPO and Realme phones. Only useful if you own one.

hagezi_samsung_tracker_blocklist.note: Samsung's device and TV telemetry. Only useful if you own Samsung hardware.

hagezi_vivo_tracker_blocklist.note: Telemetry endpoints baked into Vivo phones. Only useful if you own one.

hagezi_windows_office_tracker_blocklist.note: Windows and Office telemetry endpoints. Some Microsoft features quietly depend on these, so introduce it and then watch.

hagezi_xiaomi_tracking_blocklist.note: Telemetry endpoints baked into Xiaomi phones. Only useful if you own one.

no_google.note: Blocks every Google domain, YouTube included. This breaks a great deal of the web on purpose -- take it literally.

perflyst_dandelion_sprout_smart_tv_block.note: Stops smart TVs reporting what you watch, and blocks ads in TV apps. Small and worth having if a TV is on the network.

shadowwhisperers_dating_list.note: Dating sites and apps. A household policy list rather than a privacy or security one.

ukrainian_security_filter.note: Phishing and fraud aimed at Ukrainian users. Small, and additive to a general security list.

CHN_adrules.note: Broad coverage for Chinese sites and apps. Large enough to work as the general list on a China-facing network.

CHN_anti_ad.note: A privacy-leaning Chinese list. A reasonable alternative to AdRules; running both together is redundant.

HUN_hufilter.note: Hungarian sites. Tiny, so treat it as a supplement to an international list.

IDN_abpindo.note: Indonesian and Malaysian sites. Designed to complement a general list rather than replace one.

KOR_list_kr.note: A DNS-shaped cut of the Korean filter list. Add it beside an international list.

KOR_youslist.note: Korean sites, maintained separately from filterslist-KO. Either one works as the regional supplement.

LIT_easylist_lithuania.note: Lithuanian sites, and its own authors call it small and lightly tested. Expect little from it.

NOR_dandelion_sprouts_anti_malware_list.note: Nordic-language sites, covering both ads and malicious domains.

POL_cert_polska_list_of_malicious_domain.note: The official CERT Polska warning list, which Polish ISPs block by law. Authoritative, and large for a regional list.

POL_polish_filters_for_pi_hole.note: Polish sites. Small; pair it with the CERT Polska list for security cover.

SWE_frellwit_swedish_hosts_file.note: Swedish sites, covering ads, tracking and scams in one small list.

TUR_turk_adlist.note: Turkish sites, including the usual on-page annoyances.

TUR_turkish_ad_hosts.note: Aimed at Turkish mobile apps rather than websites. Useful beside turk-adlist, not instead of it.

VNM_abpvn.note: Vietnamese sites, and substantial for a regional list.

dandelion_sprouts_anti_malware_list.note: A general malware and phishing list, actively maintained. A sound second list beside a general ad blocker.

hagezi_badware_hoster_blocklist.note: Free hosting services that get abused to serve malware. Blocking them can also take out legitimate files hosted there.

hagezi_dns_rebind_protection.note: A dozen rules that stop public names resolving to private addresses. Cheap protection, but it will break any service that deliberately does this, such as some smart-home bridges.

hagezi_dyndns_blocklist.note: Dynamic DNS providers, which phishing campaigns lean on heavily. Do not add it if you reach your own machines through one.

hagezi_encrypted_dns_vpn_tor_proxy_bypas.note: Stops devices routing around Sift via public DoH, VPNs, Tor and proxies. A control measure, and one that will annoy anyone who uses a VPN legitimately.

hagezi_the_worlds_most_abused_tlds.note: Blocks whole top-level domains with the worst abuse records. Blunt by nature -- legitimate sites in those TLDs go too.

hagezi_threat_intelligence_feeds.note: The broadest security list here by a wide margin, merged from many threat feeds. Costs real memory for the coverage -- see the size before adding it.

hagezi_url_shortener_blocklist.note: URL shorteners, which hide where a link really goes. Expect shortened links in mail and chat to stop working -- that is the point.

urlhaus_filter_online.note: Live malware distribution hosts from abuse.ch's URLhaus. Small, current, and a good complement to a broader security list.

nocoin_filter_list.note: In-browser cryptocurrency miners. Tiny and entirely safe to add.

phishing_army.note: A large, phishing-only list. One of the better single additions if phishing is your main concern.

curben_phishing_filter.note: Phishing domains drawn from PhishTank and OpenPhish. Overlaps Phishing Army considerably; one of the two is usually enough.

scam_blocklist_by_durablenapkin.note: Scam and fake-shop domains. Small, and aimed at fraud rather than malware.

shadowwhisperers_malware_list.note: Malware, unwanted programs, browser hijackers and phishing in one list. A solid general-purpose security choice.

staklerware_indicators_list.note: Command-and-control domains used by stalkerware on phones. Small, specific, and worth having on a family network.

the_big_list_of_hacked_malware_web_sites.note: Otherwise ordinary sites that are currently compromised. Because it tracks a moving target, keep the update interval short.

ublock_badware_risks.note: uBlock Origin's own list of sites documented to put users at risk. Small, carefully curated and rarely wrong.

hostsvn.note: The most widely used Vietnamese blocklist, covering ads and tracking on Vietnamese sites and apps. Larger and more actively maintained than ABPVN; either works, both together is redundant.

kboghdadys_youtube_ads_blocklist.note: YouTube's ad-serving hostnames, for the TVs and consoles a browser extension cannot reach. Ads share googlevideo.com with the videos, so some get through and a clip occasionally will not play.
